# Get-InactiveAccount

Reports user accounts that have not signed in for a given number of days.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| **Changes the system** | No, read-only |
| **Supports `-WhatIf` / `-Confirm`** | Not needed (read-only) |
| **Admin rights** | AD permissions in AD mode; none for simulation/CSV mode |
| **PowerShell** | Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7+ |
| **Source** | [scripts/Get-InactiveAccount.ps1](https://github.com/lucaswsanchez/helpdesk-kb/blob/main/scripts/Get-InactiveAccount.ps1) &middot; [tests](https://github.com/lucaswsanchez/helpdesk-kb/blob/main/tests/Get-InactiveAccount.Tests.ps1) |

## Description

Inactive accounts (leavers never deprovisioned, test accounts, old contractors) are a common security finding. This script lists accounts whose last logon is older than -DaysInactive, or that never signed in, with a recommended action for the monthly review.

Data sources:

- Active Directory (default): uses Get-ADUser with LastLogonDate. Requires the ActiveDirectory (RSAT) module.
- CSV (-InputCsv): an export with SamAccountName, Name, Enabled, LastLogonDate and optional Department/WhenCreated columns. Use the sample file to try the script without a domain.

The script only reads data; it never disables or deletes accounts.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-DaysInactive` | Int32 | `90` | Number of days without sign-in to consider an account inactive. Default 90. |
| `-InputCsv` | String |  | Read accounts from a CSV file instead of Active Directory. |
| `-SearchBase` | String |  | In AD mode, the OU distinguished name to search. Default: whole domain. |
| `-IncludeDisabled` | switch |  | Also report accounts that are already disabled. |
| `-ReferenceDate` | DateTime | `(Get-Date)` | Date to measure inactivity from. Default: now. Useful for reproducible reports and tests. |
| `-OutputPath` | String |  | Optional path of a CSV file to export the report. |

## Examples

```powershell
.\Get-InactiveAccount.ps1 -InputCsv .\samples\ad-users.csv
```

Runs against the sample data (no domain needed).

```powershell
.\Get-InactiveAccount.ps1 -DaysInactive 60 -SearchBase 'OU=Users,OU=Acme,DC=acme,DC=example' -OutputPath .\inactive.csv
```

Lists accounts in the Users OU inactive for 60+ days and exports the report.

## Notes

LastLogonDate (lastLogonTimestamp) replicates with a delay of up to 14 days by design, so it is accurate enough for 30+ day reviews. Works on Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7+. Related KB: KB-021 Employee Offboarding.
